# charts-rs

> Pure-Rust, zero-browser charting and Mermaid diagram library: render 28 chart types plus `MultiChart` composition (29 default type names, 30 with `mermaid`) and 13 Mermaid diagram types to SVG — and optionally PNG, JPEG, WebP, or AVIF — from typed Rust APIs or validated JSON documents.

`charts-rs` (`#![forbid(unsafe_code)]`, Rust 1.88+, edition 2024) has no headless browser or Node.js dependency. Core SVG rendering is fast (tens of microseconds per chart) and ships with 10 built-in themes, custom font loading (TTF/OTF/TTC, including CJK), strict JSON schema validation with typo suggestions and structured multi-issue reporting, resource bounds (`RenderLimits`), named GeoJSON map registration, and machine-readable discovery/schema APIs designed for MCP servers and LLM tool calling.

## Installation & Feature Flags

```toml
[dependencies]
# Core pure-Rust SVG rendering (28 chart types + MultiChart, minimal deps)
charts-rs = "2"

# Add pure-Rust Mermaid rendering (13 diagram types, zero extra dependencies)
charts-rs = { version = "2", features = ["mermaid"] }

# Add per-format raster export (uses resvg + image; pick only what you need)
charts-rs = { version = "2", features = ["mermaid", "png"] }
```

- `default` (none): 28 core chart types + `multi` composition (29 type names), pure SVG output, JSON validation, Draft 2020-12 JSON Schema (`Essential` / `Full`), & unified dispatch APIs.
- `mermaid`: Pure-Rust Mermaid parser & SVG renderer (13 canonical diagram types + 7 aliases, zero extra dependencies).
- `png`, `jpeg`, `webp`, `avif`: Per-format raster encoders (`svg_to_png`, `svg_to_jpeg`, `svg_to_webp`, `svg_to_avif`); `avif` pulls in `rav1e`.
- `image-encoder`: Umbrella feature enabling `png`, `jpeg`, `webp`, and `avif`.

## Quickstart

### Typed Rust API

```rust
use charts_rs::BarChart;

let mut chart = BarChart::new(
    vec![("Email", vec![120.0, 132.0, 101.0]).into()],
    vec!["Mon".into(), "Tue".into(), "Wed".into()],
);
chart.title.text = "Visits".to_string();
let svg: String = chart.svg()?;
```

### Unified JSON Discovery, Schema, Validation & Dispatch APIs

```rust
use charts_rs::{
    ChartInfo, RenderLimits, SchemaLevel, chart_catalog, chart_example,
    chart_json_schema, chart_json_schema_with, get_font_families, list_chart_types,
    list_geo_json, list_themes, register_geo_json, render_chart_from_json,
    render_chart_from_value_with_limits, validate_chart_json,
    validate_chart_json_with_limits,
};

let types: &'static [&'static str] = list_chart_types(); // 29 default, 30 with `mermaid`
let catalog: Vec<ChartInfo> = chart_catalog();          // name, title, description, example
let themes: &'static [&'static str] = list_themes();     // 10 built-in themes
let fonts: Vec<String> = get_font_families()?;           // loaded font families

// Draft 2020-12 JSON Schema; descriptions, defaults, and examples come from docs/json.md.
let essential = chart_json_schema_with("bar", SchemaLevel::Essential)?; // ~1.6–4 KB
let full = chart_json_schema("bar")?;                                   // == SchemaLevel::Full
let example: Option<serde_json::Value> = chart_example("bar")?;

let options = serde_json::json!({
    "theme": "grafana",
    "x_axis_data": ["Mon", "Tue"],
    "series_list": [{"name": "Email", "data": [120, 132]}]
});
let limits = RenderLimits::default();
let issues = validate_chart_json_with_limits("bar", &options, &limits)?;
assert!(issues.is_empty());

let svg = render_chart_from_value_with_limits("bar", &options, &limits)?;
// Or from raw JSON string: render_chart_from_json("bar", &options.to_string())?;
```

### Mermaid API (`features = ["mermaid"]`)

```rust
use charts_rs::{
    MermaidCapabilities, MermaidChart, mermaid_capabilities, mermaid_to_svg,
    mermaid_to_svg_with_theme, mermaid_validate,
};

let caps: MermaidCapabilities = mermaid_capabilities(); // serde::Serialize
let src = "flowchart LR\n  A[Client] --> B@{ shape: diam, label: \"Gateway\" }\n  B -->|OK| C[(DB)]";
mermaid_validate(src)?;                          // syntax + semantic check with line numbers
let svg = mermaid_to_svg(src)?;                  // default theme, auto-sized SVG
let dark_svg = mermaid_to_svg_with_theme(src, "dark")?;

let mut chart = MermaidChart::new(src);
chart.allow_links = false;                       // disable <a> links for untrusted input
let safe_svg = chart.svg()?;
```

## Chart Selection Guide

| Data shape / intent | Chart type(s) | Primary data key(s) |
|---|---|---|
| Category comparison (vertical / horizontal) | `bar`, `horizontal_bar` | `x_axis_data`, `series_list` |
| Trend / time series / area / step / band | `line` | `x_axis_data` or `x_axis_values`, `series_list` |
| Part-to-whole / rings / Nightingale rose | `pie` | `series_list` |
| Conversion / stage drop-off | `funnel` | `series_list` |
| Correlation / bubble / regression / density | `scatter` | `series_list` (flat `[x,y,...]`) |
| Distribution / quartiles | `histogram`, `box_plot` | `series_list` / `x_axis_data` + `box_series` |
| Bridge / cumulative +/- steps | `waterfall` | `x_axis_data`, `data` |
| Financial OHLC | `candlestick` | `x_axis_data`, `series_list` (4 per category) |
| KPI single value / target vs ranges | `gauge`, `bullet` | `series_list` / `bullets` |
| Multi-metric comparison / radial bars | `radar`, `polar_bar` | `indicators` / `x_axis_data`, `series_list` |
| 2D matrix / daily calendar activity | `heatmap`, `calendar` | `x_axis_data` + `y_axis_data` + `series.data` / `data` |
| Hierarchy | `treemap`, `sunburst`, `tree` | `series_data` (recursive) |
| Directed flow / circular flow / network | `sankey`, `chord`, `graph` | `nodes`, `links` |
| Multi-dimensional / stream over time | `parallel`, `theme_river` | `x_axis_data`, `series_list` |
| Project timeline / tasks | `gantt` | `tasks` |
| Geographic choropleth / origin-destination flows | `map`, `lines` | `geo_json` (object or map name), `data` / `lines` |
| Tabular data + inline sparklines | `table` | `data` (2D cell array) |
| Stacked / aligned composite dashboard | `multi` | `child_charts` |
| Flowcharts, sequence, ER, class, state, mindmap, etc. | `mermaid` | `source` |

## Minimal JSON Examples

All 30 examples below match `docs/json.md`, pass `validate_chart_json`, and render directly:

- `bar`: `{"title_text":"Visits","radius":3,"x_axis_data":["Mon","Tue","Wed"],"series_list":[{"name":"Email","data":[120,132,101],"label_show":true},{"name":"Search","data":[220,182,191],"category":"line"}]}`
- `box_plot`: `{"x_axis_data":["Mon","Tue"],"box_series":[{"name":"Latency","data":[[655,850,940,980,1175],[672,800,845,885,1012]]}]}`
- `bullet`: `{"label_show":true,"bullets":[{"name":"Done in time (%)","value":92,"target":95,"ranges":[80,90,100],"max":100},{"name":"Wait (min)","value":12,"target":10,"ranges":[10,20,30]}]}`
- `calendar`: `{"start_date":"2024-01-01","end_date":"2024-03-31","data":[["2024-01-05",3],["2024-02-10",7],["2024-03-21",5]]}`
- `candlestick`: `{"x_axis_data":["2024-10-24","2024-10-25","2024-10-28"],"series_list":[{"name":"MA5","data":[20,34,10,38,40,35,30,50,31,38,33,44]}]}`
- `chord`: `{"link_gradient":true,"links":[{"source":"Asia","target":"Europe","value":60},{"source":"Asia","target":"Americas","value":45},{"source":"Europe","target":"Americas","value":50}]}`
- `funnel`: `{"series_label_position":"inside","series_list":[{"name":"Show","data":[100]},{"name":"Click","data":[80]},{"name":"Order","data":[20]}]}`
- `gantt`: `{"now":"2024-03-19","tasks":[{"name":"Research","category":"Plan","start":"2024-03-04","end":"2024-03-08","progress":1},{"name":"Design","category":"Build","start":"2024-03-07","end":"2024-03-22","progress":0.6},{"name":"Sign-off","category":"Build","start":"2024-03-22"},{"name":"Launch","category":"Plan","start":"2024-03-25","end":"2024-03-29"}]}`
- `gauge`: `{"min":0,"max":100,"value_formatter":"{c}%","series_list":[{"name":"CPU","data":[72]}]}`
- `graph`: `{"categories":["Team","Tool"],"nodes":[{"name":"Ann","category":0,"value":3},{"name":"Bob","category":0},{"name":"Git","category":1}],"links":[{"source":"Ann","target":"Bob","value":2},{"source":"Ann","target":"Git"},{"source":"Bob","target":"Git"}]}`
- `heatmap`: `{"x_axis_data":["12a","6a","12p"],"y_axis_data":["Sat","Sun"],"series":{"min":0,"max":10,"data":[[0,9],[1,3],[2,6],[3,8],[4,2],[5,5]]}}`
- `histogram`: `{"bin_width":5,"x_axis_title":"Height (cm)","series_list":[{"name":"Adults","data":[162.4,171,168.3,175.9,158.2,169.7,173.1,166.8]}]}`
- `horizontal_bar`: `{"x_axis_data":["Brazil","India","China"],"series_label_position":"inside","series_list":[{"name":"2023","data":[182,234,290],"label_show":true}]}`
- `line`: `{"series_smooth":true,"x_axis_data":["Mon","Tue","Wed","Thu"],"series_list":[{"name":"Email","data":[120,132,null,134],"mark_lines":[{"category":"average"}]},{"name":"Search","data":[220,182,191,234],"fill":true}]}`
- `lines`: `{"curveness":0.3,"lines":[{"name":"North","value":80,"from":[0,0],"to":[40,30]},{"name":"East","value":20,"from":[0,0],"to":[50,-10]},{"name":"South","value":50,"from":[10,20],"to":[30,-20]}]}`
- `map`: `{"label_show":true,"thresholds":[100,300],"colors":["#deebf7","#9ecae1","#3182bd"],"data":[["West",80],["East",420]],"geo_json":{"type":"FeatureCollection","features":[{"type":"Feature","properties":{"name":"West"},"geometry":{"type":"Polygon","coordinates":[[[100,20],[106,20],[107,26],[101,27],[100,20]]]}},{"type":"Feature","properties":{"name":"East"},"geometry":{"type":"Polygon","coordinates":[[[106,20],[113,21],[112,27],[107,26],[106,20]]]}}]}}`
- `mermaid`: `{"title_text":"Request Flow","source":"flowchart LR\n  A[Client] --> B{Gateway}\n  B -->|OK| C[(Database)]"}`
- `multi`: `{"gap":10,"child_charts":[{"type":"bar","x_axis_data":["Mon","Tue"],"series_list":[{"name":"Email","data":[120,132]}]},{"type":"pie","height":300,"series_list":[{"name":"Email","data":[40]},{"name":"Search","data":[38]}]}]}`
- `parallel`: `{"x_axis_data":["Price","Weight","Rating"],"series_list":[{"name":"A","data":[120,3.2,4.5]},{"name":"B","data":[90,4.1,3.8]}]}`
- `pie`: `{"rose_type":false,"radius":120,"inner_radius":60,"series_list":[{"name":"Email","data":[40]},{"name":"Search","data":[38]},{"name":"Direct","data":[32]}]}`
- `polar_bar`: `{"category_axis":"radius","round_cap":true,"y_axis_configs":[{"axis_max":100}],"x_axis_data":["Sleep","Steps","Water"],"series_list":[{"name":"Done","data":[92,74,61],"label_show":true}]}`
- `radar`: `{"indicators":[{"name":"Sales","max":6500},{"name":"Marketing","max":16000},{"name":"Support","max":30000}],"series_list":[{"name":"Budget","data":[4200,3000,20000]},{"name":"Spending","data":[5000,14000,28000]}]}`
- `sankey`: `{"link_gradient":true,"links":[{"source":"Coal","target":"Electricity","value":25},{"source":"Gas","target":"Electricity","value":15},{"source":"Electricity","target":"Homes","value":30},{"source":"Electricity","target":"Industry","value":10}]}`
- `scatter`: `{"series_symbol_sizes":[6,6],"series_list":[{"name":"Female","data":[161.2,51.6,167.5,59,159.5,49.2]},{"name":"Male","data":[174,65.6,175.3,71.8,193.5,80.7]}]}`
- `sunburst`: `{"inner_radius":30,"series_data":[{"name":"Grandpa","children":[{"name":"Uncle Leo","value":15},{"name":"Father","children":[{"name":"Me","value":5},{"name":"Brother","value":1}]}]}]}`
- `table`: `{"title_text":"NASDAQ","data":[["Name","Price","Change"],["Datadog Inc","97.32","-7.49%"],["Hashicorp Inc","28.66","-9.25%"]],"text_aligns":["left","center","right"],"body_font_weight":"bold","cell_styles":[{"indexes":[1,2],"font_color":"#fff","background_color":"#2d7c2b"}]}`
- `theme_river`: `{"x_axis_data":["Jan","Feb","Mar","Apr"],"series_list":[{"name":"News","data":[10,25,18,30]},{"name":"Sport","data":[15,12,22,16]}]}`
- `tree`: `{"orient":"TB","series_data":[{"name":"root","children":[{"name":"a","children":[{"name":"a1"},{"name":"a2"}]},{"name":"b"}]}]}`
- `treemap`: `{"series_data":[{"name":"Docs","children":[{"name":"Guides","value":6},{"name":"API","value":4}]},{"name":"Media","value":5}]}`
- `waterfall`: `{"x_axis_data":["Revenue","Cost","Tax","Profit"],"data":[[900,false],[-345,false],[-108,false],[0,true]]}`

## Error Format & Self-Correction Loop

- `Error::code(&self)` returns a stable category string: `"params"`, `"json"`, `"font_not_found"`, `"parse_font"`, `"mermaid"` (`mermaid` feature), and `"image_size"` / `"image_raw"` / `"svg_parse"` / `"image_encode"` (`raster` feature).
- `validate_chart_json` / `validate_chart_json_with_limits` collect up to 50 `ValidationIssue` entries in one pass (`serde::Serialize`):
  - `code`: `"unknown_field"` | `"invalid_type"` | `"invalid_enum"` | `"out_of_range"` | `"invalid_color"` | `"unknown_theme"` | `"unknown_map"` | `"missing_required"` | `"limit_exceeded"` | `"mermaid_syntax"`
  - `path`: dotted/indexed path (e.g. `"series_list[0].lable_show"`, `"child_charts[1].width"`, or `""` for root)
  - `message`: human-readable message (identical to `Error::Params`)
  - `expected` (optional): allowed values, type, or bound
  - `suggestion` (optional): full replacement path for typos (e.g. `"series_list[0].label_show"`)
  - `line` (optional): 1-based line number for Mermaid syntax errors
- Recommended LLM loop: `validate_chart` -> apply all `suggestion` / `expected` / `line` fixes -> retry `render_chart`.

## Server Deployment & Output Formats

- **Output format (`svg` vs `png`)**: many MCP clients cannot display raw SVG inline. Expose `format?: "svg" | "png"` (default `"png"` when the `png` feature is enabled), rasterize via `svg_to_png(&svg)`, and return PNG as MCP `image` content (base64) or SVG as `text` / resource.
- **Resource bounds**: always render untrusted requests via `render_chart_from_value_with_limits` / `render_chart_from_json_with_limits` with `RenderLimits` (defaults: `max_json_bytes: 1 MiB`, `max_canvas_side: 8192`, `max_data_points: 100_000`, `max_mermaid_source: 64 KiB`).
- **Fonts & CJK**: unregistered `font_family` names are NOT rejected — they remain in the SVG while text width measurement silently falls back to `"Roboto"`. Load CJK fonts at server startup with `add_fonts(&[...])`, expose `get_font_families()` via `charts://fonts`, and optionally patch `properties.font_family.enum` in returned schemas.
- **Named GeoJSON maps**: preload maps once at startup with `register_geo_json(name, geojson)` so models pass `"geo_json": "<name>"` instead of giant polygons (China province/city GeoJSON files live under `asset/geo/china/` in the repository, excluded from the published crate).
- **Async HTTP isolation**: chart rendering and PNG rasterization are synchronous CPU tasks; run them inside `tokio::task::spawn_blocking` with a request timeout, and set `allow_links = false` on untrusted Mermaid diagrams.

## MCP Integration Recipe

Recommended MCP server surface backed by `charts-rs`:

1. `list_chart_types()` -> returns `chart_catalog()` (`name`, `title`, `description`, `example`).
2. `get_chart_schema(chart_type: string, level?: "essential" | "full")` -> calls `chart_json_schema_with(chart_type, level)` (default `SchemaLevel::Essential`, open `additionalProperties: true` with `examples`; use `Full` for advanced styling).
3. `validate_chart(chart_type: string, options: object)` -> calls `validate_chart_json_with_limits(chart_type, &options, &limits)` returning structured `Vec<ValidationIssue>`.
4. `render_chart(chart_type: string, options: object, format?: "svg" | "png")` -> calls `render_chart_from_value_with_limits(chart_type, &options, &limits)`, optionally rasterizing with `svg_to_png`.
5. `validate_mermaid(source: string)` -> calls `mermaid_validate(source)` returning line-numbered `Error::Mermaid`.
6. `render_mermaid(source: string, theme?: string, allow_links?: bool)` -> builds `MermaidChart::new_with_theme(source, theme.unwrap_or_default())`, sets `chart.allow_links = allow_links.unwrap_or(false)`, and renders SVG (or PNG).

Recommended MCP **Resources**: `charts://themes` (`list_themes()`), `charts://fonts` (`get_font_families()`), `charts://maps` (`list_geo_json()`), `charts://mermaid/capabilities` (`mermaid_capabilities()`), `charts://examples/{type}` (`chart_example(type)`).

## Chart Types & Themes

### 30 Type Names (`list_chart_types()`)

- Cartesian & statistical: `bar`, `horizontal_bar`, `line`, `scatter`, `candlestick`, `histogram`, `box_plot`, `waterfall`, `theme_river`, `parallel`.
- Part-to-whole & radial: `pie`, `polar_bar`, `radar`, `funnel`, `gauge`, `bullet`, `sunburst`, `treemap`.
- Relational, hierarchy & matrix: `sankey`, `chord`, `graph`, `tree`, `heatmap`, `calendar`, `gantt`, `table`.
- Geospatial & flow: `map` (GeoJSON choropleth), `lines` (origin-destination flows, optional GeoJSON underlay).
- Composition & diagrams: `multi` (`MultiChart`, stacks or positions multiple `child_charts` with optional `align_plots`), `mermaid` (requires `mermaid` feature).

### 10 Built-in Themes (`list_themes()`)

`light` (default), `dark`, `ant`, `grafana`, `vintage`, `walden`, `westeros`, `chalk`, `shine`, `shadcn`. Custom themes can be registered at runtime via `add_theme(name, theme)`.

## Mermaid Specification (`features = ["mermaid"]`)

### 13 Canonical Diagrams (`supported_diagrams`) & 7 Aliases (`diagram_aliases`)

- Canonical (`supported_diagrams`): `flowchart`, `sequenceDiagram`, `stateDiagram-v2`, `classDiagram`, `erDiagram`, `mindmap`, `quadrantChart`, `pie`, `gantt`, `sankey-beta`, `xychart-beta`, `radar-beta`, `treemap-beta`.
- Aliases (`diagram_aliases`): `graph` -> `flowchart`, `stateDiagram` -> `stateDiagram-v2`, `classDiagram-v2` -> `classDiagram`, `sankey` -> `sankey-beta`, `xychart` -> `xychart-beta`, `radar` -> `radar-beta`, `treemap` -> `treemap-beta`.

### Explicitly Unsupported Diagrams (`unsupported_diagrams`)

Do not generate these — they return `Error::Mermaid`: `gitGraph`, `timeline`, `journey`, `C4Context`, `C4Container`, `C4Component`, `C4Dynamic`, `C4Deployment`, `architecture-beta`, `kanban`, `packet-beta`, `block-beta`, `requirementDiagram`, `zenuml`.

### Flowchart v11 `@{ shape, label }` Names (`v11_shapes`)

`rect` / `process` / `rectangle`, `rounded` / `event`, `stadium` / `terminal` / `pill`, `subproc` / `fr-rect` / `subprocess`, `cyl` / `cylinder` / `database` / `db`, `circle` / `circ`, `dbl-circ` / `double-circle` / `doublecircle`, `diam` / `diamond` / `decision`, `hex` / `hexagon` / `prepare`, `lean-r` / `in-out`, `lean-l` / `out-in`, `trap-b` / `priority`, `trap-t` / `manual`, `odd` / `asym` / `asymmetric`, `doc` / `document`, `docs` / `documents`, `delay` / `half-rounded-rectangle`, `tri` / `triangle` / `extract`, `flag` / `notch-pent`, `sm-circ` / `start`, `f-circ` / `junction`, `text`.

### Supported Frontmatter / `%%{init}%%` Keys (`init_config_keys`)

`theme` (`dark`, `forest`, `default`/`base`/`neutral`), `fontFamily`, `fontSize`, `flowchart.curve` (`step`/orthogonal default, `basis`/`smooth`, `linear`), `flowchart.nodeSpacing`, `flowchart.rankSpacing`, `sequence.mirrorActors`, `sequence.showSequenceNumbers`, `xyChart.showLegend`.

### Key Mermaid Features & Limitations

- Supported: default orthogonal rounded edge routing with side ports (`flowchart`, `stateDiagram-v2`, `classDiagram`, `erDiagram`); per-subgraph `direction` (when isolated from outer node edges); `accTitle` / `accDescr` SVG `<title>`/`<desc>` + ARIA attributes; `click` links with protocol allowlist (`http://`, `https://`, `mailto:`, relative; disable via `allow_links: false`); multiline Markdown strings (`` "`...`" ``); nested subgraphs, `classDef`/`class`/`style`; sequence `create`/`destroy`, `box`, `autonumber`; gantt `excludes`/`includes`/`vert`.
- Limitations: subgraph-level `direction` inside flowcharts is ignored when an edge directly connects an inner node to the outside (matching Mermaid); `themeVariables` color overrides are not supported (only `fontFamily` and `fontSize`); no HTML `<foreignObject>` (HTML tags stripped to plain SVG text); Font Awesome icons (`fa:fa-*`) are stripped; JS `click` callbacks are ignored; rough/hand-drawn look mode is not supported.

## Building a chart

### In Rust

```rust,no_run
use charts_rs::{
    BarChart, Box, SeriesCategory, THEME_GRAFANA, svg_to_png
};
let mut bar_chart = BarChart::new_with_theme(
    vec![
        ("Evaporation", vec![2.0, 4.9, 7.0, 23.2, 25.6, 76.7, 135.6]).into(),
        (
            "Precipitation",
            vec![2.6, 5.9, 9.0, 26.4, 28.7, 70.7, 175.6],
        )
            .into(),
        ("Temperature", vec![2.0, 2.2, 3.3, 4.5, 6.3, 10.2, 20.3]).into(),
    ],
    vec![
        "Mon".to_string(),
        "Tue".to_string(),
        "Wed".to_string(),
        "Thu".to_string(),
        "Fri".to_string(),
        "Sat".to_string(),
        "Sun".to_string(),
    ],
    THEME_GRAFANA,
);
bar_chart.title.text = "Mixed Line and Bar".to_string();
bar_chart.legend.margin = Some(Box {
    top: bar_chart.title.height,
    bottom: 5.0,
    ..Default::default()
});
bar_chart.series_list[2].category = Some(SeriesCategory::Line);
bar_chart.series_list[2].y_axis_index = 1;
bar_chart.series_list[2].label_show = true;

bar_chart
    .y_axis_configs
    .push(bar_chart.y_axis_configs[0].clone());
bar_chart.y_axis_configs[0].formatter = Some("{c} ml".to_string());
bar_chart.y_axis_configs[1].formatter = Some("{c} °C".to_string());

println!("{}", &bar_chart.svg().unwrap());
svg_to_png(&bar_chart.svg().unwrap()).unwrap();
```

### From JSON

Every key such a JSON document may have, for every chart — with its type,
its default and what it does — is listed in the
[JSON options reference](./json.md).

```rust,no_run
use charts_rs::{BarChart, svg_to_png};
let bar_chart = BarChart::from_json(
    r###"{
        "width": 630,
        "height": 410,
        "margin": {
            "left": 10,
            "top": 5,
            "right": 10
        },
        "title_text": "Bar Chart",
        "title_font_color": "#345",
        "title_align": "right",
        "sub_title_text": "demo",
        "legend_align": "left",
        "series_list": [
            {
                "name": "Email",
                "label_show": true,
                "data": [120.0, 132.0, 101.0, 134.0, 90.0, 230.0, 210.0]
            },
            {
                "name": "Union Ads",
                "data": [220.0, 182.0, 191.0, 234.0, 290.0, 330.0, 310.0]
            }
        ],
        "x_axis_data": [
            "Mon",
            "Tue",
            "Wed",
            "Thu",
            "Fri",
            "Sat",
            "Sun"
        ]
    }"###,
).unwrap();
println!("{}", bar_chart.svg().unwrap());
svg_to_png(&bar_chart.svg().unwrap()).unwrap();
```

### Options in Rust and in JSON

The options are the same on both paths, and this README names them by their
JSON key. In Rust the shared ones are grouped by what they belong to —
`title`, `sub_title`, `legend`, `x_axis`, `grid`, `series`, `tooltip` — and a
JSON key is the path of the field joined with `_`:

| JSON | Rust |
|------|------|
| `"title_font_size": 18` | `chart.title.font.size = 18.0` |
| `"legend_position": "bottom"` | `chart.legend.position = Some(Position::Bottom)` |
| `"x_axis_data": [...]` | `chart.x_axis.data = vec![...]` |
| `"series_label_font_color": "#333"` | `chart.series.label.font.color = "#333".into()` |
| `"tooltip_show": true` | `chart.tooltip.show = true` |

The exceptions: `x_boundary_gap` is `x_axis.boundary_gap`, `x_axis_type` is
`x_axis.kind`, the `axis_` of the keys of a y axis is left out (`"axis_min"`
is `y_axis_configs[0].min`), and the `series` object of a heatmap is
`heatmap_series` (`series` being the options of the series, on every chart).
Every JSON key is described in the [JSON reference](./json.md).

### Runnable examples

Runnable examples live in [`examples/`](../examples); each writes an `svg` file:

```bash
cargo run --example bar       # basic bar chart
cargo run --example line      # smooth line with area fill and mark line / points
cargo run --example pie       # nightingale (rose) chart
cargo run --example sunburst  # sunburst with label formatter, ring thickness, animation
cargo run --example sankey     # sankey flow diagram (nodes auto-derived from links)
cargo run --example tree       # node-link tree with curved links (LR layout)
cargo run --example histogram  # distribution of a sample over equal-width bins
cargo run --example polar_bar  # polar bars: stacked around the circle, and rings with round caps
cargo run --example chord      # chord diagram of the flows between nodes (gradient ribbons)
cargo run --example gantt      # gantt chart: a project plan with progress, milestones and today
cargo run --example map        # map of regions (GeoJSON) colored by value, in classes
cargo run --example mermaid --features mermaid  # Mermaid diagrams (flowchart, sequenceDiagram)
```

## Output

### Images

SVG output works with the default build. Raster export is opt-in, one
feature per format: `png`, `jpeg`, `webp` and `avif` enable `svg_to_png`,
`svg_to_jpeg`, … (and their `_with_size` variants). Pick only what you need —
`avif` in particular pulls in the heavyweight `rav1e` encoder:

```toml
[dependencies]
charts-rs = { version = "2", features = ["png"] }
```

`image-encoder` is the umbrella feature that turns on all four formats.

An image is as large as its chart, or as large as asked for:

```rust,no_run
use charts_rs::{BarChart, svg_to_png_with_size};
let chart = BarChart::from_json(
    r###"{"series_list": [{"name": "Email", "data": [120, 132, 101]}], "x_axis_data": ["Mon", "Tue", "Wed"]}"###,
).unwrap();
let svg = chart.svg().unwrap();

// Scale to exactly 800×400
let png = svg_to_png_with_size(&svg, Some(800), Some(400)).unwrap();

// Scale to width 800, preserve aspect ratio
let png = svg_to_png_with_size(&svg, Some(800), None).unwrap();
```

### Compact SVG

`chart.compact = true` (JSON `"compact": true`) writes the SVG the way an
optimizer would: no whitespace, relative path data with `h`/`v` shorthands,
grid lines and ticks merged into single paths, shared attributes hoisted onto
groups, defaults and long hex colors dropped. The picture is the same and the
file is typically 20–30% smaller. The same rewrite is available as
`charts_rs::compact_svg(&svg)` for output you already have.

## Data and labels

### Null data points

Use `null` in JSON arrays to represent missing data; the chart skips rendering for those positions.

```json
{
  "series_list": [{
    "name": "Sales",
    "data": [120.0, null, 101.0, null, 90.0]
  }]
}
```

In Rust, build the series with `Option<f32>` values (`None` is a missing point):

```rust
use charts_rs::Series;
let series = Series::new_nullable(
    "Sales".to_string(),
    vec![Some(120.0), None, Some(101.0), None, Some(90.0)],
);
// or via the tuple conversion
let series: Series = ("Sales", vec![Some(120.0), None, Some(101.0)]).into();
```

The legacy `NIL_VALUE` sentinel (`Series::new` / `Vec<f32>`) still works and is treated as `None`.

### Label formatters

Formatters are supported in `series_label_formatter`, `axis_formatter`, and `value_formatter` (GaugeChart).

| Placeholder | Meaning |
|-------------|---------|
| `{c}` | Data value |
| `{a}` | Series name |
| `{b}` | Category (x-axis label) |
| `{d}` | Percentage (pie / funnel) |
| `{t}` | Thousands notation (1.2K, 5.6M) |

### Overlapping data labels

`"series_label_hide_overlap": true` drops a data label that would be printed
over another one.

### Copyright lines and watermarks

Every chart takes `texts`: lines of text written over it, wherever they are
asked for.

<p align="center">
  <img src="../asset/image/texts.png" width="60%" alt="A chart with a source, a copyright line and a watermark">
</p>

```json
{
  "texts": [
    { "text": "Source: web analytics", "left": 10, "bottom": 6, "reserve": true },
    { "text": "© 2026 Example Inc.", "right": 10, "bottom": 6, "reserve": true },
    { "text": "DRAFT", "font_size": 72, "font_color": "#00000014", "font_weight": "bold", "rotate": -25 }
  ]
}
```

- A text is placed by its distances from the edges of the chart, in pixels:
  with a `left` it starts there, with a `right` it ends there, and with
  neither it is centered; `top` and `bottom` do the same from above and from
  below. Without any of them it is in the very middle, where a watermark
  goes.
- `font_size` (12 by default), `font_color` (that of the sub-title) and
  `font_weight` are its font, and `rotate` turns it by so many degrees. A
  watermark wants a color with an alpha, such as `"#00000014"`.
- The texts are written last, over everything else, and a chart leaves no
  room for them: a watermark is meant to be over the plot. A line that is to
  be below the axis, or above the title, says `"reserve": true`, and the
  chart is drawn in what is left: a text with a `top` or a `bottom` takes a
  band across there, one with a `left` or a `right` only a band down that
  side. A table, a calendar and a multi chart are larger by that room
  instead.
- In a `MultiChart` the `texts` at the top are over the whole picture, and
  those of a child over that child.
- A theme can have `texts` too: register one with your copyright line and
  every chart of that theme carries it. The `texts` of a chart stand in for
  those of its theme (`"texts": []` for none).

```rust
use charts_rs::{BarChart, TextConfig};

let mut chart = BarChart::new(
    vec![("Email", vec![120.0, 132.0, 101.0]).into()],
    ["Mon", "Tue", "Wed"].map(String::from).to_vec(),
);
chart.texts.push(TextConfig {
    text: "© 2026 Example Inc.".to_string(),
    right: Some(10.0),
    bottom: Some(6.0),
    // below the axis, not over its labels
    reserve: true,
    ..Default::default()
});
let svg = chart.svg().unwrap();
```

## Axes

### Value and time x axes

A line or bar chart spaces its points evenly by default (a category axis).
Give the points x values and the axis becomes continuous: every point sits at
its value, so irregular samples keep their real spacing.

```json
{
  "x_axis_title": "Time (UTC)",
  "y_axis_configs": [{ "axis_title": "Temperature (°C)" }],
  "x_axis_values": ["2024-03-01 00:00", "2024-03-01 00:20", "2024-03-01 04:00", "2024-03-01 12:00"],
  "series_list": [
    { "name": "Indoor", "data": [21.5, 21.8, 20.1, 24.6] },
    { "name": "Outdoor", "x_values": ["2024-03-01 02:00", "2024-03-01 11:00"], "data": [8.2, 14.9] }
  ]
}
```

- `x_axis_values` are shared by every series; a series sampled at other
  moments carries its own `x_values`.
- Date strings (`2024-03-01`, `2024-03-01 08:30`, `2024-03-01T08:30:00+08:00`)
  make it a time axis. Numbers are plain values, or unix seconds with
  `"x_axis_type": "time"`.
- Ticks fall on round values and round times. `x_axis_min` / `x_axis_max` fix
  the range, `x_axis_formatter` formats the labels (`"{c} km"`, or a pattern
  such as `"%m-%d %H:%M"` on a time axis) and `x_axis_time_offset` (minutes
  east of UTC) shows timestamps in local time.

In Rust, set `chart.x_axis.values` (`Vec<f64>`) and, for timestamps,
`chart.x_axis.kind = AxisType::Time`.

### Axis titles

`x_axis_title` is written below the x axis; `axis_title` in a y axis config
is written along that axis.

## Charts

What takes a word of explanation; the options of every chart are in the
[JSON reference](./json.md).

### Band around a line

A line series can carry a `band`: a lower and an upper bound for each point,
with the area between them filled in the color of the series — a confidence
interval, a forecast range, a daily minimum and maximum.

```json
{
  "x_axis_data": ["Mon", "Tue", "Wed", "Thu"],
  "series_list": [{
    "name": "Forecast",
    "data": [120, 132, 128, 141],
    "band": { "lower": [116, 126, 119, 129], "upper": [124, 138, 137, 153] }
  }]
}
```

```rust
use charts_rs::{Series, SeriesBand};
let mut series: Series = ("Forecast", vec![120.0, 132.0, 128.0, 141.0]).into();
series.band = Some(SeriesBand::new(
    vec![116.0, 126.0, 119.0, 129.0],
    vec![124.0, 138.0, 137.0, 153.0],
));
```

- The band follows its line: smooth when the series is smooth, on a category,
  value or time x axis, also for the line series of a bar chart. The y axis
  makes room for the bounds.
- A `null` bound leaves a gap in the band.
- A series with a band and no `data` draws the band alone (a min–max range).
- With `tooltip_show` the tooltip of a point tells its bounds, and the points
  carry `data-lower` / `data-upper`.
- The bounds are absolute values: a band is not stacked with its series.

### Bubble chart

A scatter chart with `"bubble": true` reads its series data as `[x, y, size]`
triples and scales each circle by its size (`bubble_min_size` /
`bubble_max_size` set the radius range):

```json
{
  "bubble": true,
  "series_list": [{ "name": "Asia", "data": [12, 77, 1400, 40, 84, 125] }]
}
```

### Marginal histograms

`"marginal": {}` on a scatter chart draws the distribution of its own points:
above the plot, how the x values fall, and to the right, how the y values
fall. The bins run from the axis minimum to its maximum, so each bar is
exactly over the points it counts. The histograms use this chart's axes
and its points.

```rust
use charts_rs::{MarginalHistogram, ScatterChart};

let mut chart = ScatterChart::new(vec![
    ("Female", vec![161.2, 51.6, 167.5, 59.0, 159.5, 49.2]).into(),
    ("Male", vec![174.0, 65.6, 175.3, 71.8, 193.5, 80.7]).into(),
]);
chart.marginal = Some(MarginalHistogram {
    bin_count: 8,
    ..Default::default()
});
let _svg = chart.svg().unwrap();
```

```json
{
  "marginal": { "bin_count": 8, "size": 70 },
  "series_list": [
    {"name": "Female", "data": [161.2, 51.6, 167.5, 59, 159.5, 49.2]},
    {"name": "Male", "data": [174, 65.6, 175.3, 71.8, 193.5, 80.7]}
  ]
}
```

- `size` is the height of the top histogram and the width of the right one,
  in pixels (default 64). The plot keeps at least 40 pixels.
- `bin_count` of `0` chooses the number of bins; it is never more than 40.
- Several series share the bins and are drawn over each other, in the color
  of the series. Each side is scaled to its own tallest bar.
- A bubble is one point: its size is not a value on either axis. A missing
  coordinate is left out, and so is a point that falls outside the axis.

### Density contours

`"contour": {}` on a scatter chart draws unfilled density lines of its own
points. Each series is estimated with a Gaussian kernel, and the lines are
traced under the points in the color of the series. The contours use this
chart's axes and its points.

```rust
use charts_rs::{DensityContour, ScatterChart};

let mut chart = ScatterChart::new(vec![(
    "A",
    vec![
        1.0, 2.1, 1.4, 1.8, 0.8, 2.4, 1.6, 2.0, 1.1, 1.7, 0.9, 2.2, 1.3, 2.5, 1.2, 1.9,
    ],
)
.into()]);
chart.contour = Some(DensityContour::default());
let _svg = chart.svg().unwrap();
```

```json
{
  "contour": { "levels": 4, "grid_size": 48 },
  "series_list": [
    {"name": "A", "data": [1, 2.1, 1.4, 1.8, 0.8, 2.4, 1.6, 2, 1.1, 1.7, 0.9, 2.2, 1.3, 2.5, 1.2, 1.9]}
  ]
}
```

- `levels` of `4` (the default) draws the lines at 20%, 40%, 60% and 80% of
  the highest density. `0` is those four, and there are never more than 8.
- `grid_size` is the number of cells along each axis of the density grid
  (default 64, from 16 to 128).
- The bandwidth follows the spread of the points on each axis (Scott's
  rule). A series with fewer than 8 points on the axes draws no line.
- A bubble is one point: its size is not a coordinate. A missing coordinate
  is left out, and so is a point that falls outside the axis. On a
  logarithmic axis the density is estimated in the log of the values, so
  the lines stay over the points.

### Histogram

A `HistogramChart` takes the raw sample as the series data and counts it
into equal-width bins:

```json
{
  "x_axis_title": "Height (cm)",
  "series_list": [{ "name": "Adults", "data": [162.4, 171.0, 168.3, 175.9, 158.2, 169.7] }]
}
```

- The bins are chosen from the sample (with round edges) by default;
  `bin_width` or `bin_count` set them, and `x_axis_min` / `x_axis_max` fix
  the range.
- `"percent": true` shows the share of each sample instead of a count.
- Several series share the bins and are drawn over each other; give them
  the same `stack` name to pile them up instead.

### Polar bar chart

A `PolarBarChart` draws the bars of a bar chart on polar axes. The categories
are `x_axis_data`; series sit side by side within a category, or pile up when
they share a `stack` name.

```json
{
  "inner_radius": 30,
  "x_axis_data": ["Jan", "Feb", "Mar", "Apr"],
  "series_list": [
    { "name": "North", "stack": "total", "data": [42, 38, 51, 64] },
    { "name": "South", "stack": "total", "data": [30, 34, 40, 58] }
  ]
}
```

- By default the categories go around the circle and the bars grow outwards.
  `"category_axis": "radius"` gives every category a ring instead, and the
  bars run around the circle: by default over three quarters of it for the
  largest value on the axis (`end_angle` changes that), with `"round_cap":
  true` for rounded ends.
- `start_angle` (degrees clockwise from 12 o'clock) turns the chart,
  `inner_radius` leaves a hole in the center, `radius` limits the size and
  `category_gap` (0 to 0.9, default 0.2) sets the space between categories.
- The value axis is the first of `y_axis_configs` (`axis_min`, `axis_max`,
  `axis_split_number`, `axis_formatter`); `x_axis_hidden` / `y_axis_hidden`
  hide the category and the value labels.
- `label_show`, `colors` (a color per bar), `tooltip_show` and `animation`
  work as in a bar chart.

In Rust: `PolarBarChart::new(series_list, x_axis_data)`, then
`chart.category_axis = PolarAxis::Radius`.

### Chord chart

A `ChordChart` shows who exchanges how much with whom: the nodes are arcs of
a circle, as long as the flows through them, and every link is a ribbon
across the circle, as wide at both ends as its value.

```json
{
  "link_gradient": true,
  "links": [
    { "source": "Asia", "target": "Europe", "value": 60 },
    { "source": "Asia", "target": "Americas", "value": 45 },
    { "source": "Europe", "target": "Americas", "value": 50 }
  ]
}
```

- The nodes are derived from the names in `links`, in first-seen order;
  list them in `nodes` (`{"name": ..., "color": ...}`) to fix their order or
  their colors. A link from a node to itself is allowed.
- A ribbon takes the color of its source node, or fades to the color of its
  target with `"link_gradient": true`; `link_opacity` (default 0.5) lets the
  ribbons show through each other.
- `node_width` (default 12) is the thickness of the ring, `node_gap`
  (default 3) the gap between nodes in degrees, `start_angle` turns the
  chart and `radius` limits its size.
- The labels are the node names; `series_label_formatter` can add the flow
  (`{c}`) or the share (`{d}`), e.g. `"{b} ({d})"`. `tooltip_show` and
  `animation` work as in the other charts.

In Rust: `ChordChart::new(vec![], vec![("Asia", "Europe", 60.0).into()])`.

### Gantt chart

A `GanttChart` draws tasks as bars along a time axis:

```json
{
  "now": "2024-03-19",
  "tasks": [
    { "name": "Research", "category": "Plan", "start": "2024-03-04", "end": "2024-03-08", "progress": 1 },
    { "name": "Design", "category": "Build", "start": "2024-03-07", "end": "2024-03-22", "progress": 0.6 },
    { "name": "Sign-off", "category": "Build", "start": "2024-03-22" }
  ]
}
```

- Every task has a row of its own, named after it; tasks with the same `row`
  share one (the bookings of a room, the flights at a gate) and are named on
  their bars.
- `category` colors the tasks and makes the legend, `progress` (0 to 1) shows
  how much is done, a task without an `end` is a milestone, and `now` marks
  a moment across the chart.
- The x axis is the time axis of the line chart: `x_axis_min` /
  `x_axis_max`, `x_axis_formatter` and `x_axis_time_offset` apply, and
  `"x_axis_type": "value"` makes it an axis of plain numbers.

In Rust: `GanttChart::new(vec![("Research", start, end).into()])`, with the
times as unix seconds.

### Map chart

A `MapChart` colors the regions of a map by their values. The regions are
GeoJSON that comes with the options — the library has no map data of its own:

```json
{
  "label_show": true,
  "thresholds": [100, 300],
  "colors": ["#deebf7", "#9ecae1", "#3182bd"],
  "data": [["West", 80], ["East", 420]],
  "geo_json": { "type": "FeatureCollection", "features": [] }
}
```

- `geo_json` is a `FeatureCollection` of `Polygon` and `MultiPolygon`
  geometries (holes and islands included); `data` gives the value of a
  region by its name, the property `name` of its feature (or another one,
  with `name_property`).
- The scale is the one of the heatmap: from `min_color` to `max_color`,
  through several `colors`, or in classes (`steps`, `thresholds`); it is
  shown beside the map. A region without a value is drawn in `empty_color`.
- `projection` is `mercator` (the default) or `equirectangular`.

In Rust: `MapChart::new(MapRegion::from_geo_json(text, "name")?, data)`.

**Named map registry (HTTP / MCP servers).** Instead of sending large GeoJSON
documents on every JSON request, preload them once at startup with
`register_geo_json` and reference them by name (`list_geo_json()` lists
registered names). Note that the files under `asset/geo/china` are in the
repository only and are not bundled into the published crate:

```rust,no_run
use charts_rs::{list_geo_json, register_geo_json, render_chart_from_json};

let geo: serde_json::Value = serde_json::from_str(
    &std::fs::read_to_string("asset/geo/china/100000_full.json").unwrap(),
)
.unwrap();
register_geo_json("china", geo).unwrap();
assert!(list_geo_json().contains(&"china".to_string()));
let svg = render_chart_from_json(
    "map",
    r#"{"geo_json": "china", "data": [["北京市", 100]]}"#,
)
.unwrap();
```

**Where to get the regions.** A real map needs a GeoJSON file of its
regions, which the library does not come with. Some places that have them:

| Source | What it has | Terms |
|---|---|---|
| [Natural Earth](https://www.naturalearthdata.com/) | The countries of the world and their states and provinces, at three levels of detail (1:10m, 1:50m, 1:110m); as GeoJSON in the `geojson` folder of [its repository](https://github.com/nvkelso/natural-earth-vector). | Public domain. |
| [geoBoundaries](https://www.geoboundaries.org/) | The administrative divisions of every country, level by level; as GeoJSON, simplified as well. | CC BY 4.0: say where the boundaries are from. |
| [GADM](https://gadm.org/) | The administrative areas of every country, several levels deep; in GeoJSON among other formats. | Free for academic and other non-commercial use; redistribution and commercial use need permission. |
| [DataV.GeoAtlas](https://datav.aliyun.com/portal/school/atlas/area_selector) | The provinces, cities and districts of China, as GeoJSON. The provinces and the cities of each are in this repository as downloaded, in [`asset/geo/china`](../asset/geo/china/README.md), with how they were got. | See the terms of the site. |

Before a file is used, it is worth a look:

- **Format.** What is read is GeoJSON with longitudes and latitudes in
  degrees, as its standard has them. A Shapefile or a TopoJSON file has to be
  converted, and coordinates in the metres of a projection turned back into
  degrees; [mapshaper](https://mapshaper.org/) does both.
- **Size.** Every point of every border is written into the SVG, so a file
  of several megabytes makes a picture of several megabytes. Simplify it to
  what a chart of a few hundred pixels can show:

  ```bash
  mapshaper provinces.shp -simplify 10% -o precision=0.001 provinces.geojson
  ```

- **Names.** `data` finds a region by its name, written exactly as in the
  file. Which property of a feature holds the name differs from source to
  source — `name`, `NAME`, `NAME_1`, `shapeName` — so look at the
  `properties` of a feature and give that key as `name_property`.
- **Terms.** The sources have terms of their own, as the table says. One
  that asks to be named can be, in a line of
  [`texts`](#copyright-lines-and-watermarks).
- **Borders.** Sources draw disputed borders differently, and some countries
  have rules for the maps that are published in them: in China a map for the
  public has to pass an official review. Check what applies before a map is
  published.

### Lines chart

A `LinesChart` draws flows from one point to another. The width of a line
is its value, between `min_width` and `max_width`. `curveness` bends each
line (`0` is straight); an arrow at the end shows the direction.

Without `geo_json` the points are on a plane. With it they are longitude
and latitude, projected like a map, and the regions are drawn underneath.

```json
{
  "curveness": 0.3,
  "lines": [
    {"name": "North", "value": 80, "from": [0, 0], "to": [40, 30]}
  ]
}
```

In Rust: `LinesChart::new(vec![((0.0, 0.0), (40.0, 30.0), 80.0).into()])`.
A fuller picture, sixteen flows over the sample country, is
`asset/lines_chart/flows.json`.

### Bullet chart

A `BulletChart` puts measures against their targets, a row each: a bar for
the value, a line across it for the target, and bands behind them for what
is poor, fair and good. Five of them take the room of one gauge, which makes
them the chart for a report of KPIs.

<p align="center">
  <img src="../asset/image/bullet.png" width="60%" alt="A bullet chart of five measures">
</p>

```json
{
  "label_show": true,
  "bullets": [
    {"name": "Done in time (%)", "value": 92, "target": 95, "ranges": [80, 90, 100], "max": 100},
    {"name": "Wait (min)", "value": 12, "target": 10, "ranges": [10, 20, 30]}
  ]
}
```

- Every row has a scale of its own, from 0 (or from below it, where a value
  is) to the first round number past its largest value, unless `min` and
  `max` say otherwise. Its ticks are round numbers.
- The bands are shades of the text color, the first one the darkest;
  `range_colors` gives them colors of their own. A measure for which less is
  better, a waiting time, wants them the other way round.
- `label_show` writes the value to the right of each row, in the format of
  `series_label_formatter`; the scales take the format of the first of
  `y_axis_configs` (`axis_formatter`), and `x_axis_hidden` leaves them out.

In Rust: `BulletChart::new(vec![("CPU", 72.0, 80.0).into()])` — a name, a
value and a target; a `Bullet` has the bands, the scale and a color as well.

### Sparklines in a table

A cell of a `TableChart` that is an array of numbers is a sparkline: a
small line of the values, drawn in place of text, from the lowest at the
bottom of the cell to the highest at the top, with a dot on the last one.

<p align="center">
  <img src="../asset/image/table-sparkline.png" width="60%" alt="A table of servers with the trend of each">
</p>

```json
{
  "data": [
    ["Server", "CPU", "Last 24 hours"],
    ["api-1", "72%", [42, 45, 51, 48, 60, 66, 63, 71, 69, 74, 70, 72]],
    ["api-2", "38%", [30, 34, 31, 29, 35, 41, null, null, 37, 38]]
  ]
}
```

- Every sparkline has a scale of its own: it shows the shape of its values,
  not how they compare with those of the other rows.
- A `null` leaves a gap. `"sparkline_type": "bar"` draws a bar for each
  value instead, from 0; `sparkline_color` colors them.
- A number in a cell is written as it is, and `null` is an empty cell.

In Rust: `table.sparklines.push(TableSparkline { indexes: vec![1, 2],
values: vec![42.0, 45.0, 51.0] })`, `indexes` being the row and the column.

### Charts one above the other

A `MultiChart` stacks its children; each draws its own axes, and the plot
of each starts after the labels of its y axis — wider for the volumes of a
stock than for its prices. With `align_plots` the plots line up: they start
where the one that starts furthest in starts and end where the one that
ends furthest in ends, so that a day is in the same place in each.

<p align="center">
  <img src="../asset/image/multi-aligned.png" width="60%" alt="Prices, volumes and MACD of a month, lined up">
</p>

```json
{
  "align_plots": true,
  "child_charts": [
    {"type": "candlestick", "height": 300, "x_axis_hidden": true, "x_axis_data": ["10-01", "10-02"],
     "series_list": [{"name": "Day", "data": [100, 101.5, 99.2, 102.1, 101.5, 99.8, 99.1, 102.4]}]},
    {"type": "bar", "height": 120, "legend_show": false, "x_axis_data": ["10-01", "10-02"],
     "series_list": [{"name": "Volume", "data": [1830000, 2240000]}]}
  ]
}
```

- It works on the bar, line, candlestick, histogram, scatter, box plot and
  waterfall children that stack; one placed by `x` and `y` keeps its plot
  where its axes put it.
- It is done with `grid_left` and `grid_right`, which every one of those
  charts takes: how far in its plot starts and ends at the least. They line
  up charts that are drawn apart, too — two SVGs on one page.
- A child that wants its plot further in (its own `grid_left`) has it
  there, and the others line up with it.

The example of the gallery is `asset/multi_chart/aligned.json`: a month of
prices with their moving averages, the volumes below them and the MACD
below those. The bars of the volumes and of the MACD are red or green with
the day (`colors` of a series, a color for each bar), and the first color
of the palette, that of the candles and the bars in the legend, is a grey.

### Mermaid diagrams

Enable the optional `mermaid` feature in `Cargo.toml` to render Mermaid diagrams
(`flowchart` / `graph`, `sequenceDiagram`, `stateDiagram` / `stateDiagram-v2`,
`classDiagram` / `classDiagram-v2`, `erDiagram`, `mindmap`, `quadrantChart`,
`pie`, `gantt`, `sankey-beta`, `xychart-beta`, `radar-beta` / `radar`, and
`treemap-beta` / `treemap`) to pure SVG without a browser:

```toml
[dependencies]
charts-rs = { version = "2", features = ["mermaid"] }
```

```rust
# #[cfg(feature = "mermaid")]
# {
use charts_rs::{MermaidChart, THEME_DARK, mermaid_to_svg, mermaid_validate};

let flow = r#"
---
title: Checkout Pipeline
config:
  flowchart:
    curve: linear
    nodeSpacing: 60
---
flowchart LR
  accTitle: Checkout Pipeline
  accDescr: Validates cart and writes to the database
  A["`**Client** _app_`"] --> B@{ shape: diam, label: "Gateway" }
  B -->|OK| C@{ shape: doc, label: "Receipt" }
  click A href "https://example.com/docs" "Open docs" _blank
"#;

// Validate syntax and semantics (with line numbers and typo hints) before rendering.
mermaid_validate(flow).unwrap();
let svg = mermaid_to_svg(flow).unwrap();
assert!(svg.starts_with("<svg"));

// Disable emitted <a> links when rendering untrusted input (also supported in JSON via `"allow_links": false`).
let mut safe_chart = MermaidChart::new(flow);
safe_chart.allow_links = false;
assert!(!safe_chart.svg().unwrap().contains("<a href="));

let mut chart = MermaidChart::new_with_theme(
    "sequenceDiagram\n  Alice->>Bob: Hello!\n  Bob-->>Alice: Hi!",
    THEME_DARK,
);
chart.width = 720.0;
let _themed_svg = chart.svg().unwrap();
# }
```

- **Auto-sizing & scaling**: `flowchart`, `sequenceDiagram`, `stateDiagram`,
  `classDiagram`, `erDiagram`, and `mindmap` size automatically to fit the
  diagram when `width` and `height` are `0.0`; setting either scales
  proportionally via `viewBox`.
- **Validation & diagnostics**: `mermaid_validate(source)` runs preprocessing,
  syntax parsing, and semantic checks (such as Sankey cycle detection and
  all-zero Pie validation) across all 13 diagram types, returning line-numbered
  `Error::Mermaid` diagnostics with typo suggestions (e.g. `stateDiagram-v3` ->
  `stateDiagram-v2`, or `->>` inside a flowchart).
- **Frontmatter & `%%{init}%%` config passthrough**: supports `title`,
  `config.theme`, `config.fontFamily`, `config.flowchart.{curve, nodeSpacing,
  rankSpacing}` (`basis` / `linear` / `step`), `config.sequence.{mirrorActors,
  showSequenceNumbers}`, and `config.xyChart.showLegend`. Explicit Rust / JSON
  API options take precedence over frontmatter and `%%{init}%%`.
- **Edge routing**: flowchart, state, class and ER edges default to orthogonal
  routes with rounded corners. Edges leave and enter nodes through the sides
  facing the layout direction and are spread evenly along flat sides.
  `curve: basis` switches flowcharts to smooth splines (still leaving nodes
  perpendicularly); `curve: linear` keeps straight center-to-center lines;
  `curve: step` is the same as the orthogonal default.
- **Subgraph direction**: `direction TB|BT|LR|RL` inside a flowchart
  `subgraph` lays that subgraph out in its own direction as a composite block
  (nesting supported). As in Mermaid, it is ignored when an edge links one of
  the subgraph's inner nodes to the outside; edges to the subgraph itself are
  fine.
- **Accessibility & safe links**: `accTitle:` and `accDescr:` / `accDescr { ... }`
  emit `role="img"`, `aria-labelledby`, `aria-describedby`, `<title>`, and
  `<desc>` on the root `<svg>`. `click` / `link` directives in `flowchart`,
  `classDiagram`, and `stateDiagram` wrap nodes in `<a href="...">` using a
  strict protocol allowlist (`http://`, `https://`, `mailto:`, and relative
  URLs; `javascript:` / `data:` are blocked), and can be disabled globally via
  `chart.allow_links = false` or JSON `"allow_links": false`.
- **Rich syntax**: styling inherits from the active `charts-rs` theme
  (`THEME_DARK`, `THEME_SHADCN`, …) and supports `style`, `classDef`, `class`,
  `:::`, `linkStyle`, v11 `A@{ shape: doc, label: "..." }` node shapes,
  multiline Markdown strings (`` "`...`" `` with `**bold**` and `*italic*`),
  and `gantt` `excludes` / `includes` / `weekday` / `tickInterval` / `vert`
  markers.
- **Composition**: `MermaidChart` implements [`Chart`](https://docs.rs/charts-rs)
  and can be composed inside `MultiChart` (`"type": "mermaid"`).

## Fonts

```rust,no_run
use charts_rs::add_fonts;
let buf = std::fs::read("path/to/font.ttf").unwrap();
add_fonts(&[&buf]).unwrap();
```

A font is known by the names of its family, in every language it gives them
in: `"font_family": "PingFang SC"` and `"苹方-简"` are the same font. Every
face of a collection (`.ttc`) is registered, and text is measured with the
regular face of a family. `get_font_families()` lists the names.

A `font_family` that is not registered is still written to the SVG (the
viewer resolves it), but text is measured with the default font.

A font is kept as its bytes and its glyphs are read as text is measured with
them, so a large CJK font costs no more memory than its file.

**Server / HTTP deployment.** When serving charts with CJK text, preload a
CJK font once at startup via `add_fonts` and expose `get_font_families()` to
clients or MCP tools. Without loaded CJK fonts, text width measurement falls
back to `Roboto` (producing inaccurate label spacing) and raster export (`png`,
etc.) may render missing glyphs.

## Development

The SVG output is covered by snapshot tests under `asset/`. After an
intentional rendering change, regenerate them and review the diff:

```bash
UPDATE_SNAPSHOTS=1 cargo test --features image-encoder
UPDATE_SNAPSHOTS=1 cargo test --features "mermaid,image-encoder" --test mermaid
git diff --stat asset/
```

---

# JSON options

[中文](./json-zh.md)

Every chart can be created from a JSON document with its `from_json`, e.g. `BarChart::from_json(json)`. This page lists every key such a document may have.

- A key that is left out, or set to `null`, keeps its default.
- The document is checked before it is used: an unknown key (with a hint when it looks like a typo), a value of the wrong type, an unknown enum value or a size out of range is an error, not silently ignored.
- Enum values are matched without regard to case.
- “theme” as a default means the value comes from the theme.
- The names of the keys are the names of the fields of the chart structs, so the [API documentation](https://docs.rs/charts-rs) tells the same story for the builder API.

## Contents

- [Value types](#value-types)
- [Common options](#common-options)
- Charts: [Bar](#bar), [Horizontal bar](#horizontal-bar), [Line](#line), [Pie](#pie), [Radar](#radar), [Scatter](#scatter), [Candlestick](#candlestick), [Table](#table), [Heatmap](#heatmap), [Funnel](#funnel), [Waterfall](#waterfall), [Calendar](#calendar), [Gauge](#gauge), [Bullet](#bullet), [Treemap](#treemap), [Box plot](#box-plot), [Sunburst](#sunburst), [Sankey](#sankey), [Tree](#tree), [Graph](#graph), [Parallel](#parallel), [Theme river](#theme-river), [Histogram](#histogram), [Polar bar](#polar-bar), [Chord](#chord), [Gantt](#gantt), [Lines](#lines), [Map](#map), [Mermaid](#mermaid), [Multi chart](#multi-chart)
- [Keys for tools](#keys-for-tools)

## Value types

| Type | Written as |
|---|---|
| number | Any JSON number. |
| integer | A whole number, not negative. Counts of ticks and splits go up to 1000, indexes up to 1 000 000. |
| color | `"#rgb"`, `"#rgba"`, `"#rrggbb"`, `"#rrggbbaa"`, `"rgb(r, g, b)"`, `"rgba(r, g, b, a)"` or `"transparent"`. |
| margin | A number for all four sides, or `{"left": 5, "top": 5, "right": 5, "bottom": 5}` (sides left out are `0`). |
| scale | `"linear"`, `"log"` (base 10), `"log2"`, `"log10"`, or `{"type": "log", "base": 5}`. |
| x value | A number, or a date as a string: `"2024-03-01"`, `"2024-03-01 08:30"`, `"2024-03-01T08:30:00+08:00"`. Numbers on a time axis are unix seconds. |
| number[] | An array of numbers; `null` is a missing value. |
| color[] | An array of colors; `null` keeps the default of that position. |

## Common options

These keys are accepted by every chart except the table and the multi chart. A chart uses the ones that mean something for it: a pie chart has no axes, for instance, and ignores the axis keys.

<!-- keys: base -->

### Canvas

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `theme` | string | `"light"` | Name of the theme: `light`, `dark`, `ant`, `vintage`, `shine`, `walden`, `westeros`, `chalk`, `grafana`, `shadcn`, or one registered with `add_theme`. An unknown name is an error. |
| `width` | number > 0 | `600` | Width of the chart in pixels. |
| `height` | number > 0 | `400` | Height of the chart in pixels. |
| `x` | number | `0` | Horizontal offset of the chart inside the SVG. |
| `y` | number | `0` | Vertical offset of the chart inside the SVG. |
| `margin` | margin | `5` | Margin around the whole chart. |
| `font_family` | string | `"Roboto"` | Font family of every text. Unregistered names are not rejected: they stay in the SVG while text width measurement silently falls back to `"Roboto"` (see [Fonts](./guide.md#fonts)). |
| `compact` | boolean | `false` | Emits compact SVG: the same picture, typically 20–30% smaller. |
| `empty_text` | string |  | Text shown in the middle of the plot when there is no data to draw. |

### Title

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `title_text` | string |  | Title text; no title is drawn when empty. |
| `title_font_size` | number | `18` | Title font size. |
| `title_font_color` | color | theme | Title font color. |
| `title_font_weight` | string | `"bold"` | Title font weight, e.g. `"bold"`. |
| `title_margin` | margin |  | Margin around the title. |
| `title_align` | `"left"` / `"center"` / `"right"` | `"center"` | Horizontal alignment of the title. |
| `title_height` | number | `30` | Height reserved for the title row. |

### Sub-title

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `sub_title_text` | string |  | Sub-title text, drawn under the title. |
| `sub_title_font_size` | number | `14` | Sub-title font size. |
| `sub_title_font_color` | color | theme | Sub-title font color. |
| `sub_title_font_weight` | string |  | Sub-title font weight, e.g. `"bold"`. |
| `sub_title_margin` | margin |  | Margin around the sub-title. |
| `sub_title_align` | `"left"` / `"center"` / `"right"` | `"center"` | Horizontal alignment of the sub-title. |
| `sub_title_height` | number | `20` | Height reserved for the sub-title row. |

### Legend

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `legend_show` | boolean |  | Shows or hides the legend. It is shown by default, except in pie, theme river and waterfall charts. |
| `legend_position` | `"top"` / `"bottom"` / `"left"` / `"right"` | `"top"` | Where the legend goes: at the top (the default), at the bottom, or stacked vertically on the left or right of the plot. At the top it shares the row of the title where there is room for both — a title on the left and a legend on the right, say — and goes below the title and the sub-title where it would be written over them. |
| `legend_align` | `"left"` / `"center"` / `"right"` | `"center"` | Horizontal alignment of the legend. |
| `legend_category` | `"normal"` / `"rect"` / `"round_rect"` / `"circle"` | `"normal"` | Shape of the legend markers: a line with a dot (`normal`), a rectangle, a rounded rectangle or a circle. |
| `legend_font_size` | number | `14` | Legend font size. |
| `legend_font_color` | color | theme | Legend font color. |
| `legend_font_weight` | string |  | Legend font weight, e.g. `"bold"`. |
| `legend_margin` | margin |  | Margin around the legend. A legend at the top with a `top` margin is placed by it, and is not moved below the title. |

### X axis

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `x_axis_data` | string[] |  | Labels of the x axis: the categories of the chart. |
| `x_axis_type` | `"category"` / `"value"` / `"time"` | `"category"` | How the values of a continuous x axis read: plain numbers (`value`) or timestamps (`time`). The axis is continuous whenever x values are given; date strings select `time` by themselves. |
| `x_axis_values` | x value[] |  | The x value of each data point, shared by every series. Setting them makes the x axis continuous: points sit at their value instead of in evenly spaced slots (line and bar charts). |
| `x_axis_min` | x value |  | Fixed start of a continuous x axis; by default the first value. In a histogram: the start of the first bin. |
| `x_axis_max` | x value |  | Fixed end of a continuous x axis; by default the last value. In a histogram: the end of the last bin. |
| `x_axis_formatter` | string |  | Format of the x axis labels: `{c}` is the label; on a time axis a pattern of `%Y %y %m %d %H %M %S %b`, e.g. `"%m-%d %H:%M"`. |
| `x_axis_time_offset` | number | `0` | Minutes east of UTC a time axis is displayed in (480 for UTC+8). |
| `x_axis_title` | string |  | Title of the x axis, written below its labels. |
| `x_axis_hidden` | boolean | `false` | Hides the x axis. In a polar bar chart: the category labels. |
| `x_axis_height` | number | `30` | Height reserved for the x axis. |
| `x_axis_stroke_color` | color | theme | Color of the x axis line and ticks. |
| `x_axis_stroke_width` | number | `1` | Width of the x axis line and ticks. |
| `x_axis_font_size` | number | `14` | Font size of the x axis labels. |
| `x_axis_font_color` | color | theme | Font color of the x axis labels. |
| `x_axis_font_weight` | string |  | Font weight of the x axis labels, e.g. `"bold"`. |
| `x_axis_name_gap` | number | `5` | Gap between the x axis line and its labels. |
| `x_axis_name_rotate` | number | `0` | Rotation of the x axis labels in radians, e.g. `0.785` for 45°. |
| `x_axis_margin` | margin |  | Margin around the x axis. |
| `x_boundary_gap` | boolean | `true` | Leaves a gap at both ends of the x axis, so points sit in the middle of their category (`true`), or puts the first and last point on the ends of the axis (`false`). |
| `x_axis_label_overflow` | `"thin"` / `"rotate"` / `"ellipsis"` | `"thin"` | What to do with x axis labels that do not fit side by side: leave some out (`thin`), rotate them, or cut them with an ellipsis. |

### Y axis

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `y_axis_hidden` | boolean | `false` | Hides the y axis. In a polar bar chart: the value labels. |
| `y_axis_configs` | object[] |  | The value axes: the first one is the left y axis, a second one the right y axis. |

### Grid

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `grid_stroke_color` | color | theme | Color of the grid lines. |
| `grid_stroke_width` | number | `1` | Width of the grid lines. |
| `grid_stroke_dash_array` | string |  | Dashes of the grid lines, as the `stroke-dasharray` of SVG takes them (e.g. `"4,2"`). Solid lines by default. Applies to the grid of the charts with an x and a y axis, to those of the gantt, radar and polar bar charts, to the lines of a punch card and to the axes of a parallel chart. |
| `grid_left` | number |  | How far from the left edge of the chart the plot starts, at the least: further in than the y axis puts it, so that the plots of charts one above the other line up (see `align_plots` of a multi chart). Where the axis needs more the plot starts where the axis puts it. In bar, line, candlestick, histogram, scatter, box plot and waterfall charts; the histogram to the right of the plot of a scatter chart stays against the plot. |
| `grid_right` | number |  | How far from the right edge of the chart the plot ends, at the least, as `grid_left` does on the other side. |

### Series

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `series_list` | object[] |  | The data series of the chart. |
| `series_colors` | color[] | theme | The color palette: a series takes the color at its position, starting over when the palette runs out. |
| `series_stroke_width` | number | `2` | Stroke width of the series lines. |
| `series_symbol` | object |  | Marker drawn on the data points of every line, and on the vertices of a radar polygon; `null` draws none. On a line the default is a circle as large as `series_stroke_width`, filled with the background color. A radar chart that leaves this and every series `symbol` unset keeps a circle of radius 2 on each vertex. |
| `series_smooth` | boolean | `false` | Draws line series as smooth curves. |
| `series_fill` | boolean | `false` | Fills the area under line series. |
| `series_fill_opacity` | number |  | How opaque the fill of an area is, from 0 to 1. Default: `0.39` under a line, `0.2` in a radar chart. |
| `series_label_formatter` | string |  | Format of the data labels: `{c}` value, `{a}` series name, `{b}` category, `{d}` percentage, `{t}` value in thousands notation. |
| `series_label_font_size` | number | `14` | Font size of the data labels. |
| `series_label_font_color` | color | theme | Font color of the data labels. |
| `series_label_font_weight` | string |  | Font weight of the data labels, e.g. `"bold"`. |
| `series_label_hide_overlap` | boolean | `false` | Leaves out a data label that would overlap one already drawn. |
| `stack_percent` | boolean | `false` | Shows the series of a stack as their shares of it: every stack adds up to 100%, on an axis in percent (bar, horizontal bar, line and polar bar charts). |

### Tooltip and animation

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `tooltip_show` | boolean | `false` | Gives every data shape a tooltip that shows on hover (plain CSS, no script), and a `<title>` for assistive tools. Not available in calendar, gauge, parallel, radar and theme river charts. |
| `tooltip_font_size` | number |  | Font size of the tooltips. Default: that of the data labels (`series_label_font_size`). |
| `tooltip_font_color` | color |  | Font color of the tooltips. Default: that of the data labels (`series_label_font_color`). |
| `tooltip_font_weight` | string |  | Font weight of the tooltips, e.g. `"bold"`. None by default. |
| `texts` | object[] |  | Texts written over the chart, each wherever it is asked for: a copyright line, a watermark. See [`texts[]`](#texts). A theme may have texts as well; these stand in for them. |
| `animation` | object |  | Animates the chart as it appears; `{}` uses the defaults. Supported by the bar, horizontal bar, line, pie, funnel, sunburst, treemap, sankey, histogram, polar bar and chord charts. |

### `series_list[]`

<!-- keys: base.series_list -->

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string |  | Name of the series, shown in the legend and in tooltips. |
| `data` | number[] |  | The values of the series, one per category; `null` is a missing point. Some charts read them differently, as told in their sections. |
| `index` | integer ≥ 0 |  | Position in the color palette; by default the position of the series. |
| `y_axis_index` | integer ≥ 0 | `0` | The y axis the series belongs to: `0` (left) or `1` (right). |
| `label_show` | boolean | `false` | Shows the value of every data point as a label. |
| `category` | `"line"` / `"bar"` |  | In a bar chart: draws this series as a line (`line`) instead of bars. |
| `start_index` | integer ≥ 0 | `0` | Index of the category the first value belongs to. |
| `mark_lines` | object[] |  | Lines across the plot at a statistic of the series or at a fixed value. |
| `mark_points` | object[] |  | Markers on points of the series, each with the value of its point in it: on the smallest, on the largest, or on any one by its index. A series that is drawn as a line has them. |
| `mark_areas` | object[] |  | Shaded bands across the plot between two values. |
| `colors` | color[] |  | A color for each data point (bar, horizontal bar and polar bar charts); `null` keeps the color of the series. |
| `stroke_dash_array` | string |  | Dash pattern of a line series, and of a radar polygon, e.g. `"4 2"`. |
| `stack` | string |  | Name of a stack: series with the same name (and y axis) are piled on top of each other. |
| `smooth` | boolean |  | Overrides `series_smooth` for this series. |
| `fill` | boolean |  | Overrides `series_fill` for this series. |
| `symbol` | object |  | Overrides `series_symbol` for this series; `null` draws no marker. Used by line series and radar polygons. |
| `x_values` | x value[] |  | The x value of each data point, for a series that is not sampled at the chart’s `x_axis_values`. |
| `band` | object |  | A filled band around the line: a lower and an upper bound for each data point. |
| `step` | `"start"` / `"middle"` / `"end"` |  | Draws the line as steps: level between two points, changing to the next value at the point itself (`start`), half way to the next one (`middle`) or at the next point (`end`). Wins over `smooth`. |
| `error_bar` | object |  | Error bars: a lower and an upper bound for each data point, drawn as a line with a cap at both ends over the bar or the point (bar, line and scatter charts). The y axis makes room for them, and tooltips tell the bounds. |
| `ring` | integer ≥ 0 | `0` | In a pie chart: the ring the series is a slice of. The series of a ring share a circle of their own, the lowest ring innermost — nested pies. |

#### `series_list[].mark_lines[]`

<!-- keys: base.series_list.mark_lines -->

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `category` | `"average"` / `"min"` / `"max"` / `"value"` |  | Where the line is drawn: at the average, the minimum or the maximum of the series, or at `value`. |
| `value` | number |  | The value of the line when `category` is `value`. |
| `color` | color |  | Color of the line, its dot and its arrow. Default: the color of the series. |
| `stroke_width` | number | `1` | Width of the line. |
| `stroke_dash_array` | string | `"4,2"` | Dashes of the line, as the `stroke-dasharray` of SVG takes them; `""` draws a solid line. |

#### `series_list[].mark_points[]`

<!-- keys: base.series_list.mark_points -->

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `category` | `"min"` / `"max"` / `"index"` |  | The point that is marked: the smallest value of the series, the largest, or the one whose `index` is given. |
| `index` | integer |  | With the `"index"` category, which point: its place in the `data` of the series, the first one being 0. A point without a value has no marker. |

A marker is above its point and as large as the value in it; the plot starts lower where one would reach above it. Two peaks of a day are the largest value and one more point:

```json
{
  "mark_points": [
    { "category": "max" },
    { "category": "index", "index": 28 }
  ]
}
```

#### `series_list[].mark_areas[]`

<!-- keys: base.series_list.mark_areas -->

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `from` | number / `"average"` / `"min"` / `"max"` |  | One edge of the band. |
| `to` | number / `"average"` / `"min"` / `"max"` |  | The other edge of the band. |
| `color` | color |  | Color of the band. Default: the color of the series. |
| `opacity` | number | `0.16` | How opaque the band is, from 0 to 1. A `color` with an alpha of its own (`"#ff000080"`) keeps it when no opacity is given. |

#### `series_list[].symbol` and `series_symbol`

<!-- keys: base.series_list.symbol -->
<!-- keys: base.series_symbol = base.series_list.symbol -->

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `type` | `"circle"` / `"rect"` / `"square"` / `"triangle"` / `"diamond"` / `"none"` |  | Shape of the marker (`square` is the same as `rect`); `"none"` draws no marker, as `null` does. |
| `size` | number |  | Size of the marker: its radius, or half its side. |
| `radius` | number |  | The same as `size`, which wins when both are set. |
| `color` | color |  | Fill color of the marker; without one the marker is hollow. |

#### `series_list[].band`

<!-- keys: base.series_list.band -->

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `lower` | number[] |  | Lower bound of each point; `null` leaves a gap in the band. |
| `upper` | number[] |  | Upper bound of each point; `null` leaves a gap in the band. |

#### `series_list[].error_bar`

<!-- keys: base.series_list.error_bar -->

The same two lists as a band: a point has an error bar where both of its bounds are given.

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `lower` | number[] |  | Lower end of the error bar of each point; `null` leaves the point without one. |
| `upper` | number[] |  | Upper end of the error bar of each point; `null` leaves the point without one. |
| `stroke_width` | number | `1.5` | Width of the error bars. |

### `y_axis_configs[]`

<!-- keys: base.y_axis_configs -->

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `axis_font_size` | number | `14` | Font size of the axis labels. |
| `axis_font_color` | color | theme | Font color of the axis labels. |
| `axis_font_weight` | string |  | Font weight of the axis labels, e.g. `"bold"`. |
| `axis_stroke_color` | color | `transparent` | Color of the axis line; transparent by default. |
| `axis_stroke_width` | number | `1` | Width of the axis line and ticks. |
| `axis_width` | number |  | Width reserved for the axis; by default as wide as its labels need. |
| `axis_split_number` | integer 0–1000 | `6` | Number of intervals the value range is split into. |
| `axis_name_gap` | number | `8` | Gap between the axis line and its labels. |
| `axis_formatter` | string |  | Format of the axis labels: `{c}` value, `{t}` value in thousands notation, e.g. `"{c} ms"`. |
| `axis_margin` | margin |  | Margin around the axis. |
| `axis_min` | number |  | Fixed lower bound of the axis; by default derived from the data. |
| `axis_max` | number |  | Fixed upper bound of the axis; by default derived from the data. |
| `axis_scale` | scale | `"linear"` | Scale of the axis: linear or logarithmic. |
| `axis_title` | string |  | Title of the axis, written along it. |
| `axis_inverse` | boolean | `false` | Turns the axis upside down: the smallest value at the top, the largest at the bottom (a ranking, where 1 is the best place). |

### `texts[]`

<!-- keys: base.texts -->
<!-- keys: table.texts = base.texts -->
<!-- keys: mermaid.texts = base.texts -->
<!-- keys: multi.texts = base.texts -->

A text is placed by its distances from the edges of the chart, in pixels. With a `left` it starts there, with a `right` it ends there, and with neither it is centered; `top` and `bottom` do the same from above and from below. It is written last, over everything else — and over a part of the chart, where it is put on one. A text that is to have room of its own, such as a line of sources below the axis, asks for it with `reserve`.

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `text` | string |  | The text, on one line. An entry without text is left out. |
| `left` | number |  | Distance of the start of the text from the left edge. |
| `top` | number |  | Distance of the top of the text from the top edge. |
| `right` | number |  | Distance of the end of the text from the right edge. `left` wins where both are given. |
| `bottom` | number |  | Distance of the bottom of the text from the bottom edge. `top` wins where both are given. |
| `font_size` | number | `12` | Font size of the text. |
| `font_color` | color | theme | Font color of the text; by default that of the sub-title. A watermark wants a color with an alpha, e.g. `"#00000020"`. |
| `font_weight` | string |  | Font weight of the text, e.g. `"bold"`. |
| `rotate` | number | `0` | Degrees the text is turned by, clockwise, about the point it is placed by: its start, its end or, centered, its middle. |
| `reserve` | boolean | `false` | Makes room for the text at the edge it is placed from, instead of writing it over the chart: the chart is drawn in what is left, with its `margin` inside of that. A text with a `top` or a `bottom` takes a band across there, as far in as it reaches (`bottom` and its font size, say); one with a `left` or a `right` only takes a band down that side, as wide as it is. Two at an edge take the room of the one that reaches further in. A text in the middle has no edge to take room at. A table, a calendar and a multi chart, which are as large as what is in them, are larger by the room. |

```json
{
  "texts": [
    { "text": "© 2026 ACME Inc.", "right": 10, "bottom": 6, "reserve": true },
    { "text": "CONFIDENTIAL", "font_size": 56, "font_color": "#00000018", "rotate": -25 }
  ]
}
```

### `animation`

<!-- keys: base.animation -->

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `duration` | integer ≥ 0 | `1000` | Duration of the animation in milliseconds. |
| `easing` | string | `"ease"` | CSS easing function: `ease`, `linear`, `ease-in`, `ease-out`, `ease-in-out`. |
| `delay` | integer ≥ 0 | `80` | Delay in milliseconds between one element and the next (bars, series, slices, levels). |

## Bar

`BarChart::from_json` — Vertical bars, one group per category of `x_axis_data`. A series with `"category": "line"` is drawn as a line; series with the same `stack` pile up; `y_axis_index` binds a series to the right y axis.

<!-- keys: bar -->

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `radius` | number |  | Corner radius of the bars. |
| `series_label_position` | `"top"` / `"inside"` | `"top"` | Where the value labels of the bars go: above their end, or in the middle of the bar, which suits stacked bars (and is the default with `stack_percent`). |

<!-- example: bar -->

```json
{
  "title_text": "Visits",
  "radius": 3,
  "x_axis_data": ["Mon", "Tue", "Wed"],
  "series_list": [
    {"name": "Email", "data": [120, 132, 101], "label_show": true},
    {"name": "Search", "data": [220, 182, 191], "category": "line"}
  ]
}
```

## Horizontal bar

`HorizontalBarChart::from_json` — Horizontal bars: the categories of `x_axis_data` go down the left side, the values along the bottom.

<!-- keys: horizontal_bar -->

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `series_label_position` | `"left"` / `"right"` / `"top"` / `"bottom"` / `"inside"` | `"right"` | Where the value labels go; by default to the right of the bars. |

<!-- example: horizontal_bar -->

```json
{
  "x_axis_data": ["Brazil", "India", "China"],
  "series_label_position": "inside",
  "series_list": [
    {"name": "2023", "data": [182, 234, 290], "label_show": true}
  ]
}
```

## Line

`LineChart::from_json` — Lines over the categories of `x_axis_data`, or over a continuous x axis when `x_axis_values` are given. It has no keys of its own: smooth curves, steps, area fill, markers, mark lines and bands are all [common options](#common-options).
